title: Ethiopian Amete Mihret Calendar
intro: The Ethiopian Amete Mihret calendar is a living civil and religious chronology used in Ethiopia.
epoch: Amete Mihret means Years of Mercy. Its Christian-era numbering differs from the Gregorian era by approximately seven or eight years, depending on the date.
structure: The first twelve months contain thirty days each. Pagume, the thirteenth, contains five days in ordinary years and six in the Alexandrian-style four-year leap cycle.
example: After Nehase 30 comes Pagume; after its final day the year begins at Meskerem 1. In contemporary Gregorian dates this usually falls on 11 or 12 September.
history: The calendar descends from the Alexandrian tradition. Its months remain central to Ethiopian civil and religious life, including Enkutatash (New Year).
model: The provider implements the Amete Mihret arithmetic chronology; the month/day fields and period navigation refer to the same underlying day.
limits: Not interchangeable with the separate Amete Alem era or the Ethiopian clock convention. Gregorian correspondences shift over long historical ranges.
